subject: Re: Demo request — concurrency & latency for label-generation pipeline
messages:
From: Amandeep Kaur <amandeep@parcelgrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@parcelgrid.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Demo request — concurrency & latency for label-generation pipeline

Hi Hannah,

We signed up via the self-serve flow and I'd like to set up a short demo to understand Redwood's performance reliability for a label-generation use case. Quick context: ParcelGrid builds shipping orchestration for mid-market retailers. We're evaluating LLM inference to populate address-normalization, customs summaries, and a compact "shipping-note" text block printed on labels.

Estimated traffic profile:
- Average: ~200 req/s (each request is a single address + order metadata; ~80-180 tokens)
- Peak burst: up to ~1,000 req/s for short windows (90-120s) during batch label prints
- Typical latency target: p95 <= 150ms; p99 ideally < 300ms for the single-request path

Timeline: aiming for a beta rollout in Q4 2027; decision window over the next 6–8 weeks.

Questions we want you to cover in the demo:
1) What deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated) make sense for consistent p99 under bursts?
2) How does caching / prefix caching help with label templates?
3) Typical batch size tradeoffs for reducing cost without violating latency SLOs
4) Any requirements for test traffic (format/sample) so we can iterate quickly

I've attached a small CSV with a sample of our address payloads (traffic-sample.csv) and included Raj (eng) who would join the call. Can you share a few available slots? Prefer mornings PST next week.

Thanks,
Amandeep
Amandeep Kaur
Product Lead, ParcelGrid
amandeep@parcelgrid.com

Attachment: traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 78KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Amandeep Kaur <amandeep@parcelgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — concurrency & latency for label-generation pipeline

Hi Amandeep — thanks for the context and for attaching the sample. Quick answers up front and a couple of qualification items so we prep the right demo: 

- We can absolutely show hosted vs dedicated performance tradeoffs; for the burst profile you described many customers prefer a dedicated pool with burst capacity or a hybrid routing policy.
- Prefix/KV caching is effective for repeated templates; we'll show an example during the demo.
- Batch-size guidance varies by model and SLO; we'll bring suggested configs tailored to your token lengths.

Could you confirm the following before we lock a slot?
1) Expected concurrency per single worker if you shard the print job (e.g., do you plan to fan-out 1:1 requests or batch them server-side?)
2) Any data residency / customer data handling constraints (PCI/HIPAA/PII policies)?
3) Are you evaluating quantized models (we can cover 8-bit/4-bit tradeoffs) or only full-precision for now?
4) Who from engineering (name + email + timezone) will join so we can include a brief infra-deep-dive?

Proposed times (PST):
- Tue 4/20 10:00–10:30
- Wed 4/21 09:00–09:30
- Thu 4/22 11:30–12:00

Or you can pick any open 30-min slot here: https://calendly.com/redwood-demo/30min?event=parcelgrid

Attaching a 1-page demo agenda and checklist so everyone knows what we'll cover.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
SDR, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachment: demo-agenda.pdf (PDF, 34KB)
From: Amandeep Kaur <amandeep@parcelgrid.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@parcelgrid.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo request — concurrency & latency for label-generation pipeline

Thanks Hannah — answered inline below.

> 1) Expected concurrency per single worker if you shard the print job?
We typically fan-out at the orchestration layer with small batches of 8–16 addresses, but we also have flows that do 1:1 requests for real-time single-label printing at kiosks. So demo please cover both batching and single-request latency.

> 2) Any data residency / customer data handling constraints?
US-only data residency is preferred for now; we'll have PII (names, addresses). No HIPAA. We will require encryption at rest and logs retention controls.

> 3) Are you evaluating quantized models?
We are open but prefer you to show: hosted (default), dedicated with 8bit quant, and an example of a smaller quantized variant for cost comparison.

> 4) Who from engineering will join?
Raj Patel (raj.patel@parcelgrid.com) - backend infra, PST. He can make any of the proposed times except Tue 4/20 morning.

Can we take Wed 4/21 09:00 PST? Also, is there any pre-demo perf report you can share (example p95/p99 numbers for similar customers)?

-Amandeep

--
Amandeep Kaur
Product Lead, ParcelGrid
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Hi Amandeep — Ben here (AE). Wed 4/21 09:00 PST works for us. I've tentatively booked that slot on the calendar and shared a 30-min invite.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m intros & goals
- 8m architecture & routing (hosted vs dedicated + burst policy)
- 8m live perf demo with a small sample of your traffic (we'll replay a subset of traffic-sample.csv)
- 5m config recommendations (batching, quantization, caching) + next steps

Pre-demo items for you (quick wins):
- If you can mark 100–200 representative rows in traffic-sample.csv (we'll use that file) and indicate which flows are single-request vs batch, we can repro realistic p95/p99.
- If there are any IP allowlist or VPN constraints for a private demo environment, share those now.

Sharing a short perf snapshot we can anonymize from a recent retail customer with a similar token distribution: p95 ~ 120ms (single-request hosted baseline), p99 ~ 340ms on hosted; dedicated with 8-bit quant/local batching reduced p99 to ~180ms with consistent peaks handled via burst nodes. I'll include that PDF on the call.

Thanks — see you Wed.
Ben Carter

ben_carter@redwood.com
